subject: Franska 4
title: Reading comprehension: an opinion piece
sourceSummary: A longer, opinion-driven text about social media's impact on young people, with questions that train main idea, inference, vocabulary in context, and argument analysis at a more advanced level.

questions.prompt:
Read the text:

"Faut-il interdire les réseaux sociaux aux moins de seize ans ? La question divise. D'un côté, plusieurs études pointent un lien entre l'usage intensif des écrans et une hausse de l'anxiété chez les adolescents. De l'autre, les principaux concernés rappellent que ces plateformes sont devenues un espace essentiel de socialisation, surtout pour les jeunes isolés géographiquement ou marginalisés. Interdire, disent-ils, ne ferait que déplacer le problème vers des applications moins régulées, échappant à tout contrôle parental."

What is the text mainly about?
questions.opener: Look for the question posed in the first sentence — the rest of the text answers it.
choices: Whether social media should be banned for under-sixteens
How to regulate internet use in schools
Why teenagers are geographically isolated
Which apps are most popular among young people
questions.explanation: The text opens with the question "Faut-il interdire les réseaux sociaux aux moins de seize ans ?" (Should social media be banned for under-sixteens?) and the whole text weighs arguments for and against that question.

questions.prompt:
Read the text again (see the previous question).

What argument do opponents of a ban use?
questions.opener: Read the sentence that starts with "De l'autre" (on the other hand).
choices: That studies on screen time are unreliable
That social media is an important social platform, especially for isolated or marginalized young people
That parents already have full control over their children's screen time
That a ban would be too expensive to enforce
questions.explanation: The text says that "les principaux concernés rappellent que ces plateformes sont devenues un espace essentiel de socialisation, surtout pour les jeunes isolés géographiquement ou marginalisés" — social media serves an important social function for precisely these groups.

questions.prompt:
Read the text again.

In the sentence "Interdire, disent-ils, ne ferait que déplacer le problème vers des applications moins régulées, échappant à tout contrôle parental", what does "échappant à" mean?
questions.opener: The context describes unregulated apps — what do they do in relation to parental control?
choices: which require
which support
which escape/evade
which improve
questions.explanation: "Échapper à" means to escape or evade something. Apps that are "moins régulées" (less regulated) and "échappant à tout contrôle parental" are apps that evade all parental control — essentially impossible to monitor.

questions.prompt:
Read the text again.

Why does the text specifically mention "les jeunes isolés géographiquement ou marginalisés"?
questions.opener: Think about what kind of argument this strengthens.
choices: To show that the ban would be illegal
To give a concrete example of who would lose the most from a ban
To prove that social media causes anxiety
To explain why apps are poorly regulated
questions.explanation: By pointing to a specific, vulnerable group, the text makes the counterargument more concrete and emotionally convincing — it's not just "young people in general" who would be affected, but especially those who are already isolated or marginalized.

questions.prompt:
Read the text again.

How would you describe the structure of the text?
questions.opener: Look at how "D'un côté" and "De l'autre" are used.
choices: It presents only one perspective and argues strongly for it
It tells a personal story without taking a position
It weighs two opposing perspectives against each other without clearly taking a side
It lists statistics without any argumentation at all
questions.explanation: The phrase pair "d'un côté... de l'autre" (on one hand... on the other hand) signals a balanced structure where the text presents arguments from both sides without explicitly taking a position.

questions.prompt:
Read the text again.

What does "un lien" mean in "plusieurs études pointent un lien entre l'usage intensif des écrans et une hausse de l'anxiété"?
questions.opener: The word describes the relationship between two things the studies examined.
choices: a solution
a connection
a difference
a threat
questions.explanation: "Un lien" means a connection or link. The studies "pointent un lien entre l'usage intensif des écrans et une hausse de l'anxiété" — they point to a connection between intensive screen use and increased anxiety (without necessarily proving cause and effect).

questions.prompt: Summarize the text's two main arguments (for and against a ban) in your own words, and explain why the text avoids taking a clear stance.
questions.opener: First identify which two sentences carry each argument, then phrase them briefly.
questions.answer: For a ban: screen time may increase anxiety in young people. Against a ban: social media is an important social space, especially for vulnerable youth, and a ban would just shift the problem to unregulated apps. The text balances both without taking a side.
steps: The argument for a ban is in the first half: "plusieurs études pointent un lien entre l'usage intensif des écrans et une hausse de l'anxiété chez les adolescents" — a concern about mental health, grounded in research.

The argument against a ban is in the second half: social media serves a social function, especially for "les jeunes isolés géographiquement ou marginalisés", and a ban risks pushing young people toward apps that are "échappant à tout contrôle parental" — worse, not better.

The text's structure ("d'un côté... de l'autre") and word choices ("la question divise", "disent-ils") show that the writer deliberately stays neutral and lets both sides' voices be heard, rather than arguing for a conclusion.
This is typical of an opinion piece that aims to inform and add nuance rather than persuade — a technique worth recognizing in upper-secondary-level reading comprehension.

questions.prompt: Which strategies help you analyze a longer, opinion-driven French text at upper-secondary level?
questions.opener: Going beyond just understanding the words, to understanding the text's structure.
questions.answer: Identify the question/thesis the text revolves around, often in the first paragraph. Look for structural markers like "d'un côté / de l'autre", "cependant", "toutefois", "en revanche" — they show where the argument turns. Distinguish between facts (études, statistiques) and opinions (disent-ils, selon certains). Ask yourself whether the text takes a clear stance or deliberately balances perspectives — word choices like "la question divise" signal the latter. For difficult words: use the context, especially the word or phrase right before/after. Summarize each paragraph's main point in one sentence before answering detail questions.

questions.prompt:
Read the text: "Le télétravail, longtemps marginal en France, s'est imposé durablement dans de nombreux secteurs depuis la crise sanitaire de 2020. Ses partisans mettent en avant un meilleur équilibre entre vie professionnelle et vie personnelle, ainsi qu'une réduction du temps de trajet, souvent source de fatigue et de stress. Certaines entreprises constatent même une hausse de la productivité chez les salariés qui travaillent depuis leur domicile. Toutefois, plusieurs experts en ressources humaines s'inquiètent d'un effet pervers : l'isolement social. Privés des échanges informels de la pause-café ou du déjeuner entre collègues, certains employés rapportent un sentiment de solitude, voire un désengagement progressif vis-à-vis de leur entreprise. Par ailleurs, les managers peinent parfois à évaluer la charge de travail réelle de leurs équipes à distance, ce qui peut conduire, paradoxalement, à un surinvestissement plutôt qu'à un relâchement. Face à ces constats contrastés, de nombreuses entreprises optent désormais pour un modèle hybride, combinant jours de télétravail et présence au bureau, dans l'espoir de conserver les avantages des deux formules."

What is the text mainly about?
questions.opener: Read the whole text and weigh the advantages, drawbacks, and conclusion together.
choices: The pros and cons of remote work, and the hybrid model many companies are now choosing
Instructions on how to apply for remote work
The history of internet development in France
A description of a specific French company
questions.explanation: The text weighs advantages (balance, productivity) against drawbacks (isolation, hard-to-assess workload) and concludes that many companies are now opting for a hybrid model.

questions.prompt: Same text. Which argument do supporters of remote work use?
questions.opener: Look for the sentence starting with "Ses partisans mettent en avant...".
choices: A better work-life balance and reduced commuting time
That it's cheaper for employees
That it bans meetings entirely
That offices are closing permanently
questions.explanation: The text says supporters highlight "un meilleur équilibre entre vie professionnelle et vie personnelle" and "une réduction du temps de trajet".

questions.prompt: Same text. What does "un effet pervers" mean in the context of the experts' concern?
questions.opener: "Pervers" here doesn't mean the same as the common English sense — it refers to an unexpected, negative consequence.
choices: An unintended negative side effect
A positive surprise
A legal problem
A financial gain
questions.explanation: "Un effet pervers" means an unintended, negative side effect of something that might otherwise seem positive.

questions.prompt: Same text. What is the critics' main concern about remote work, according to the text?
questions.opener: Look for the sentences about "l'isolement social" and "la charge de travail".
choices: Social isolation and difficulty assessing workload remotely
That home internet is too slow
That remote work is illegal
That wages are dropping
questions.explanation: The text mentions both "l'isolement social" and that managers "peinent... à évaluer la charge de travail réelle" (struggle to assess the real workload).

questions.prompt: Same text. What can be inferred about why the difficulty of assessing workload might lead to "surinvestissement" (overworking) rather than relaxation?
questions.opener: Think about what happens when an employee doesn't know if they're doing enough.
choices: Without clear oversight, employees may feel pressure to work more to prove their productivity
Employees always get less work when remote
Managers always give too little work
Remote work always legally requires overtime
questions.explanation: When managers struggle to assess workload, employees may compensate by working more than necessary to demonstrate commitment, leading to overworking rather than relaxation.

questions.prompt: Same text. What solution are many companies choosing today, according to the last sentence?
questions.opener: Read the last sentence about "un modèle hybride".
choices: A hybrid model combining remote work and office presence
Abolishing remote work entirely
Abolishing office work entirely
Letting each employee decide completely freely
questions.explanation: The text says many companies "optent désormais pour un modèle hybride, combinant jours de télétravail et présence au bureau".

questions.prompt: Same text. What does "la charge de travail" mean?
choices: The workload
The workplace
The salary
The working hours
questions.explanation: "La charge de travail" means the workload, how much work a person is expected to do.
